tagline: Down the French Broad under the palisades to Marshall.
intro: Monticello Road leaves US 25/70 in Weaverville, just off I-26, and within three miles hands the trip to NC 251, the Old Marshall Highway, which comes down to the French Broad and follows it west. Sheer rock walls, palisades the wide river cut over time, line the right side of the road. Past the Ivey River bridge it becomes Main Street in Marshall, and the byway ends at the US 25/70 bypass beyond town, sixteen miles from the start.

The way was first a Native American trading path toward the Tennessee and Ohio valleys. Settlers widened the paths into roads, and when the trains came, the river valley was again the path of least resistance.

moments.title: Vance Birthplace
moments.text: Zebulon Vance, the state's Civil War governor, was born in 1830 on this Reems Creek farm, where eighteen enslaved people lived and worked.

moments.title: Marshall
moments.text: Madison County people describe their county seat as a block wide, a mile long, sky high and hell deep, pinned between the river and the mountains with one bridge across.
